Why Apple Inc (NASDAQ:AAPL) Is A Buy When Markets Go Down Andrew Edmonds February 7, 2018 
When stocks are plummeting in price, it’s hard to start buying into all the uncertainty. But a disciplined long term investor knows there’s no better time to buy than right now. And I’m not talking about buying into speculative, high-risk stocks. I’m talking about the well-proven, robust track record Apple Inc. Why? Size. Financial health. Proven performance. Check out our latest analysis for Apple 
Apple Inc. designs, manufactures, and markets mobile communication and media devices, and personal computers to consumers, and small and mid-sized businesses; and education, enterprise, and government customers worldwide. Founded in 1977, and led by CEO Timothy Cook, the company currently employs 123,000 people and with the company’s market cap sitting at US$814.38B, it falls under the large-cap stocks category. Volatility in the market is hardly detrimental to the financial health and business operations of a large, well-established company. Although some monetary and fiscal policy changes may impact some corporate financing decisions and strategy, what we’ve learnt over time is that these companies tend to adapt. And having a strong balance sheet and a history of proven success aids in this adaptability. NasdaqGS:AAPL Historical Debt Feb 7th 18 
With US$122.40B debt on its books, Apple has to pay interest periodically. This means it needs to have enough cash on hand to meet these upcoming expenses. Apple generates enough earnings to cover its interest payments, its interest expenses are also covered by interest income, and furthermore, its operating cash flows amply covers its total debt by 52.82%, which is higher than the bare minimum requirement of 20%. Its cash and short-term investment is also sufficient to cover other upcoming liabilities, which means AAPL is financially robust in the face of a volatile market. NasdaqGS:AAPL Income Statement Feb 7th 18 
AAPL’s year-on-year earnings growth has been positive over the past five years, with an average annual growth rate of 8.15%, beating the market growth rate of 7.93%. It has also returned an ROE of 37.07% recently, above the industry return of 8.40%. This consistent market outperformance illustrates a robust track record of delivering strong returns over a number of years, increasing my conviction in Apple as an investment over the long run. Next Steps: Based on these three factors, AAPL makes for a strong long-term investment in the face of a fickle stock market. If you’re a risk averse investor, lining your portfolio with proven companies you’re willing to buy more and more of as the price falls, is a good strategy to build your wealth over the long run.
